article.name: AMITY / Archangel-8
article.summary: AMITY is a local Python session-memory and CovenantVault implementation paired with a C++ sensory/orchestration layer and optional ZeroMQ IPC. The curated repository locator currently returns 404; this review uses the same-owner public Amity-v2.0 repository as the current AMITY candidate and records lineage as unresolved.

who_what.text: The reviewed artifact is a public source repository rather than a hosted memory service. Its README presents Python session, memory and ethics code alongside C++ sensory/orchestration code and optional ZeroMQ IPC. The inspected paths do not establish production deployment or physical sensor integration.

architecture.text: Python SessionState stores a required pilot_signature, timestamps, bounded sensory and episodic deques, sample_count and a sensory overflow counter. SensorReading contains timestamp, profile, frequency, friction and temperature; EpisodicMemory contains timestamp, event_type and an arbitrary content dictionary. Defaults cap sensory samples at 1,000 and episodes at 20,000.

Orchestrator8 dispatches packets to sensory, emotional, memory and sovereignty handlers. MemoryArtery appends an episode for packets with priority tier at least 7. Sensory deque overflow is counted before its oldest item is displaced; the episodic deque has no matching overflow counter.

The C++ master owns sensory, flavor, emotional, simulation, ingress, emitter-lock, sandbox, sovereignty and IPC components, plus sensory/flavor/emotional ring buffers. Its UnifiedTelemetry returns energy, boundary, sensory buffer pressure, emitter lock, simulation state and emotional warmth. The inspected code does not show a shared persistent store between C++ buffers and Python episodes.

behavior.text: Session writes append to bounded deques. save_to_file serializes the retained state as JSON; its default atomic mode writes a temporary file, flushes and fsyncs it, then replaces the destination. Periodic saving is opt-in and defaults to a 60-second interval. load_from_file reconstructs state and derives pilot_signature from the file rather than from a separately supplied expected identity.

daily_recall(days) scans the episode deque and filters by timestamp cutoff; it does not search or rank text. CovenantVault recall scans entries by category and age. generate_briefing orders SACRED, PERMANENT and PROMISE before the top-valence JOY and DAILY entries, then truncates to max_memories.

CovenantVault remember appends a list-length ID, timestamp, content, category, valence, tags and source string, then rewrites the JSON vault. Unknown categories become DAILY. decay_check physically removes expired entries; recall merely omits expired entries. No general episode update or delete API was found in the inspected methods.

The vault requires a constructor pilot signature and rejects a loaded pilot value that differs. Session buffers have no tenant, user or project scope argument. A source string on vault records and arbitrary episode payloads do not establish validated provenance or claim-level evidence.

The ZeroMQ bridge serializes telemetry as JSON. The inspected C++ telemetry handler looks for a sensory_reading substring and constructs a fixed sample packet rather than parsing the JSON payload. The README also describes IPC as stubbed unless ZeroMQ is linked; interoperability was not executed or verified.

metrics.evidence: Timestamp cutoff and vault-category retrieval are visible, but no AMITY outputs were captured or adjudicated against eligible answerable or unanswerable probes.
No general update or supersession API was found in the inspected session/vault methods, and no correction probes were run.
Vault decay_check prunes expired records, but no explicit user-directed delete path was found in the inspected memory API and no post-delete probes were run.
A pilot signature is retained and checked by the vault loader, but no cross-principal or cross-file isolation probes were captured.
Vault source is a string and episode content is caller-defined; no outputs were adjudicated for source support or citation coverage.
No AMITY request timings or scheduled write-to-recall probes were collected.
No model usage, token accounting, or cost measurement was collected for this review.
JSON persistence is visible in source, but stored bytes and bytes per accepted item were not measured.

limits.text: This is a bounded, read-only source review at the recorded SHA. It did not run or build AMITY, run tests, exercise the IPC or persistence paths, or inspect every repository component. Source and README claims do not establish correctness, concurrency safety, hardware behavior, security, reliability, or performance.

The curated Sovereign locator currently returns 404. The owner profile and current Amity-v2.0 repository expose a matching AMITY identity, but the inspected public pages do not prove direct repository lineage; this review records that uncertainty explicitly.

benchmark.text: Status: Benchmark not run for AMITY. No AMITY runtime, benchmark workload, tests, or build were run. Shared metric definitions and fixture describe the protocol; the execution-status record contains no AMITY result, and planned fixture counts are not measurements.
